key_insight: Training vision models with a human-like developmental visual diet shifts them to rely more on shape than texture, producing substantially more robust and resource-efficient visual inference.
problem_solved: Brings a practical solution to the fragility of modern vision models that over-rely on texture and fail under realistic distortions or distribution shifts, without needing massive compute or specialised robustness training.
method: Design a training ‘visual diet’ that mimics stages of human visual development (progressive, naturalistic exposures rather than static large-scale sampling).
Train standard vision architectures on this developmental curriculum and compare feature reliance (shape vs texture) and robustness to distortions and distribution shifts.
Evaluate robustness and efficiency to show improved shape bias and better generalisation under noise, occlusion and domain changes with lower resource cost.
impact: Provides AI/ML practitioners a practical, data- and curriculum-based recipe to improve model robustness and shape-based representations without heavy compute or adversarial interventions — useful for reliable deployment in real-world settings.
visual_elements: Before/after comparison: two example images with model attention maps showing texture-dominated vs shape-dominated features.

paper_title: Adopting a human developmental visual diet yields robust and shape-based AI vision
paper_authors: Zejin Lu, Sushrut Thorat, Radoslaw M. Cichy, Tim C. Kietzmann
